text:
sara: FYI — I pushed a prototype for regional warm-pool steering to the router configs. Need quick review on header handling and spoofing risk.

mike: warm-pool? how different from regular failover?

sara: warm pool = small set of prewarmed inference nodes in failover regions (e.g., eu-west) that we route to if local can't meet 90ms SLO. reduces cold-starts vs spinning up on demand.

lee: config sample?

sara: ```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "match": {"tenant": "*"},
  "prefer_local": true,
  "warm_pool": {
    "enabled": true,
    "regions": ["us-west-2", "eu-west-1"],
    "latency_budget_ms": 25
  },
  "headers": {
    "preserve": ["Authorization", "X-Request-ID"],
    "strip": ["X-Region-Override"]
  }
}
```

mike: strip X-Region-Override makes sense to avoid client spoofing. But some customers rely on it for region pinning.

anya: can we honor tenant-level allowlist? e.g., per-tenant flag that lets header through if tenant.trust === true.

sara: exactly what I had in mind — per-tenant header whitelist + console toggle. default = strip. We need telemetry showing how often header used.

lee: add metrics: routing.origin_hinted_region and routing.chosen_region, and a tag warm_pool_used:true/false.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for router-v2 -> staging :rocket:

mike: also thinking about TTL on warm-pool nodes and cost. If warm_pool used a lot in eu-west we should scale dedicated pool.

anya: I'll add a console UX ticket: "Tenant header override allowlist + warm-pool toggle" and a rollout flag. link: https://go/redwood/infra/PR-456

sara: action items: 1) implement per-tenant whitelist (anya), 2) telemetry (lee), 3) default strip X-Region-Override (sara), 4) doc for operators about warm-pool sizing (mike). :thumbsup:

lee: +1
mike: +1
anya: on it
